claims.text: The high-entropy transition-metal oxide has higher OER activity than corresponding single-cation catalysts.
The enhanced OER activity is caused by dynamic, synergistic redistribution of oxidation states among chemically distinct transition-metal cations during intermediate adsorption.
Dynamic redistribution of cation oxidation states optimizes intermediate binding energies and turnover rates.
LaCr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2O3-δ can be prepared as an epitaxial (001) perovskite oxide film.
Single-B-site parent perovskites provide compositionally simpler comparators for the high-entropy perovskite.
The high-entropy and single-B-site films can be compared with identical morphology and surface termination.
Multiple transition-metal cations in the high-entropy matrix dynamically switch valence under OER operation.
Dynamic multication valence switching creates synergistic interactions at surface active sites.
Several metal centers undergo simultaneous oxidation and reduction when OER intermediates adsorb.
Multication synergy produces an optimal distribution of binding energies for intermediates such as OH*.
The proposed binding-energy distribution lowers OER kinetic barriers and increases activity.
Under identical OER conditions, the high-entropy oxide will exhibit substantially higher current density than its single-B-site comparators.
The high-entropy oxide will show measurable, reversible oxidation-state shifts in several cations during OER.
The corresponding single-B-site perovskites roughly follow traditional volcano-type OER activity trends.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to epitaxial perovskite oxides under aqueous OER conditions when morphology and crystallographic facet are controlled.
Surface reconstruction at different pH values or high overpotentials may compete with the proposed multication mechanism.
